title: Rockenfeller leads from pole to win Moscow Race 2
dek: Mike Rockenfeller converted pole into a lights-to-flag win, 4.132 seconds clear of Bruno Spengler, while Mattias Ekström climbed from fifth to third and took the championship lead back.

chapters.title: Saturday's fallout sets up the hour-long race
text: Saturday had belonged to Pascal Wehrlein, who passed pole-sitter Marco Wittmann with about four minutes left in Race 1 and took the championship lead on 119 points, eight ahead of Mattias Ekström. The Swede had been out of the race since a lap 11 collision with Timo Glock, and the stewards gave him a three-place grid penalty for Sunday. Audi's mechanics worked through the night to rebuild his car and Miguel Molina's, both damaged on Saturday.

Sunday's race ran for an hour and every car had to make a pit stop, so tyre life and the quality of the stops mattered as much as grid position. With Wehrlein, Ekström and Edoardo Mortara separated by only 13 points at the top, the race offered a chance to take control of the title fight.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller goes from 14th to pole
text: Mike Rockenfeller had been 14th and 0.470 seconds off the pace on Saturday, but he put his Phoenix Audi on pole with a 1m28.540s lap. He said the car had finally come together after a lacklustre year and that the field was so close that a couple of tenths could drop a driver out of the top ten.

Ekström was second quickest, 0.038 seconds behind, but his penalty dropped him to fifth on the grid and promoted Bruno Spengler to the front row. Maxime Martin's BMW started third and Jamie Green's Audi fourth, with Nico Müller sixth. Gary Paffett, 20th on Saturday, qualified seventh and was the best of the Mercedes drivers.

The margins were small. Wittmann, who held the top of the times for much of the session, was just 0.146 seconds from pole and still only tenth. Wehrlein, the points leader, managed only 11th, 0.199 seconds off, and shared the sixth row with Daniel Juncadella. Antonio Giovinazzi, in his second qualifying as Timo Scheider's stand-in, started from the back of the grid, with Martin Tomczyk 23rd.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller holds off Spengler into Turn 1
text: Rockenfeller made a poorer start than Spengler, who was on his inside, and took a risk by turning in to keep the place. It worked, and he led the field away. Behind them the BMW of Martin tried to get past Spengler, ran off the track, and Green almost took both of them before settling in third, with Martin fourth and Ekström fifth.

DRS was enabled after four laps, but Rockenfeller was already more than a second clear, so Spengler as first chaser had no DRS to attack with and spent the opening stint defending from Green, Martin and Ekström in a close, bumper-to-bumper group. Further back, Giovinazzi went through the gravel and rejoined, and Wehrlein, who lost a place to Mortara early on, spent several laps trying to get back ahead of the Audi driver.

chapters.title: A slow stop costs Green, and Auer holds up the pack
text: Green was among the first to stop, but a front wheel did not come off cleanly and he rejoined behind Martin, who pitted a lap later, and behind Ekström, who stopped five laps after Green. That ended Green's plan of using a quicker out-lap to catch Spengler. At the stops Mortara also got ahead of Wehrlein again.

Lucas Auer took his stop last, and his old tyres held up the group of Spengler, Martin, Ekström and Green for a long time. Spengler got past at the end of lap 21, the others needed several more laps and passed on the straight, and Auer came in on the following lap. By then Spengler had opened a gap of more than three seconds over his pursuers.

chapters.title: Ekström passes Martin for the podium
text: Ekström had said after Saturday's crash that he had learned patience, and he stayed behind Green and Martin until the last stage. About ten minutes from the end he braked late at the end of the long straight, went through at the last corner and took third place from Martin, who had defended for several laps and was praised by his team on the radio. Green tried the same on Martin on the last lap but remained fifth.

Rockenfeller took the flag 4.132 seconds ahead of Spengler, with Ekström 9.204 seconds behind the winner. He also set the fastest lap on lap 21. Martin was fourth, Green fifth and Paffett sixth, the best Mercedes, ahead of Wittmann, Mortara and Müller. Wehrlein, who had started 11th, came home tenth, collecting the single remaining point. Tomczyk, who started 23rd, was the only retirement.

chapters.title: Ekström leads again after Rockenfeller's Moscow win
text: Rockenfeller said the car was exactly what he needed and was quick despite the extra ballast it carried, and that it had been a rollercoaster weekend after a poor Saturday. He called the result a big relief for himself and his team after difficult weeks. The start, he explained, was the only anxious moment, and from then on he could manage the race without much pressure. Spengler called it a hard race and said the early duels meant he could not stay with the leader, but he was pleased to hold second.

Ekström said Saturday had been a wake-up call and that he had been more cautious this time, adding that without his grid penalty he would have liked to fight Rockenfeller for the win. His mechanics had rebuilt the Audi overnight. Wehrlein said that starting 11th had decided his race: the team had not been good enough in qualifying, and there was little to be gained after that. His tenth place left him chasing Ekström rather than leading the table.

The result put Ekström back on top of the standings with 126 points. Wehrlein was second on 120, Mortara third on 110 and Green fourth on 103, with Spengler fifth on 85 and Wittmann sixth on 75. Paffett's sixth place made him the best Mercedes finisher, while Wittmann, Saturday's pole-sitter, was seventh. Mortara's eighth place kept him within 16 points of the lead. Ekström noted that six races remained, at Oschersleben, the Nürburgring and Hockenheim, and that the title would be settled at the end of the season. Rockenfeller pointed out that 150 points were still available and expected the three remaining circuits to suit Audi.
About 26,000 spectators had attended the weekend. The DTM's next round is at Oschersleben on 11-13 September, when Races 13 and 14 of the season will be held.

facts.v: Mike Rockenfeller won over 41 laps in 1:02:14.818, 4.132 seconds ahead of Bruno Spengler.
